title: Application of Derivative

notes.heading: 1. Tangents, Normals, Subtangent & Related Rates
notes.proseLatex: At $(x_0, y_0)$ on $y = f(x)$, the tangent slope is $m_T = f'(x_0)$ with equation $y - y_0 = m_T(x - x_0)$, and the normal has slope $m_N = -1/m_T$ (vertical tangent when $1/m_T = 0$). Two curves intersect orthogonally at $P$ if $m_1 m_2 = -1$ at $P$. Related-rate problems differentiate geometric relations (such as $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ or $x^2+y^2=\ell^2$) with respect to time $t$ via the chain rule.

keyFormulas.label: Tangent, Normal & Orthogonal Curves
keyFormulas.latex: $y - y_0 = f'(x_0)(x - x_0),\quad y - y_0 = -\frac{1}{f'(x_0)}(x - x_0),\quad m_1 m_2 = -1 \text{ (orthogonal)}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Write tangent/normal equations and test orthogonal intersection of curves.

examples.problemLatex: Find the slope of the normal to $y = x^3 - 3x + 2$ at $x = 2$.
stepsLatex: Differentiate: $y' = 3x^2 - 3$, so tangent slope at $x=2$ is $m_T = 3(4) - 3 = 9$.

notes.heading: 2. Monotonicity, Concavity & Inflection Points
notes.proseLatex: On an interval $I$, $f'(x) > 0$ implies $f$ is strictly increasing and $f'(x) < 0$ implies $f$ is strictly decreasing (isolated zeros of $f'$ where sign does not flip, such as $x^3$ at $x=0$, preserve strict monotonicity!). Second derivative $f''(x) > 0$ marks upward concavity (convex) and $f''(x) < 0$ marks downward concavity; a point of inflection occurs only where concavity ACTUALLY changes sign across $x_0$.

keyFormulas.label: Monotonicity & Inflection Criterion
keyFormulas.latex: $f'(x) > 0 \implies f \uparrow;\quad f''(x_0)=0 \text{ with sign change of } f'' \implies \text{point of inflection}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Distinguish genuine inflection points from flat fourth-degree minima.

notes.heading: 3. Local vs Global Maxima & Minima
notes.proseLatex: Critical points occur where $f'(c) = 0$ or $f'(c)$ is undefined inside the domain. At a stationary point $f'(c)=0$: $f''(c) < 0$ gives a strict local maximum, $f''(c) > 0$ gives a strict local minimum, and if $f''(c)=0$ one checks the first non-zero higher derivative $f^{(k)}(c)$ (even $k$ gives extremum; odd $k$ gives inflection). On a closed interval $[a,b]$, global extrema MUST compare all interior critical values against the endpoint values $f(a)$ and $f(b)$.

keyFormulas.label: Second Derivative Test & Standard Extrema
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Apply 2nd-derivative test and recall high-frequency JELET extrema.

examples.problemLatex: Find the maximum value of $f(x) = x e^{-x}$ for $x \in [0, \infty)$.
stepsLatex: $f''(x) = e^{-x}(x - 2)$, so $f''(1) = -e^{-1} < 0$ (local & global max on $[0,\infty)$), with $f(1) = \frac{1}{e}$.

wbjeebTraps: $f''(c) = 0$ does NOT automatically mean an inflection point: for $f(x) = x^4$, $f''(0)=0$ yet $x=0$ is a strict minimum.
For $f(x) = x + \frac{1}{x}$ ($x\neq 0$), the local maximum $(-2$ at $x=-1)$ is LESS than the local minimum $(+2$ at $x=1)$ because $x=0$ splits the domain.
On a closed interval $[a,b]$, forgetting to evaluate endpoints $f(a), f(b)$ misses global maxima/minima when $f$ is monotonic.

conceptPrimer.heading: The Derivative as Slope and as Rate
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $f'(x_0)$ answers two questions with one number: the slope of the tangent to $y = f(x)$ at $(x_0, y_0)$, and the instantaneous rate $\frac{dy}{dx}$; with a parameter, the chain rule converts rates — $\frac{dY}{dt} = f'(x)\frac{dx}{dt}$. Everything in this unit is one of these two readings wearing different clothes. Micro-check: for $y = x^3 - 2x$, $y' = 3x^2 - 2$, so at $x = 1$ the tangent slope is $3(1) - 2 = 1$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Tangents & Normals on Demand
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: At $(x_0, y_0)$: tangent $y - y_0 = m_T(x - x_0)$ with $m_T = f'(x_0)$; normal $y - y_0 = m_N(x - x_0)$ with $m_N = -1/m_T$. Horizontal tangent: $m_T = 0$; vertical tangent: $m_T$ undefined. Two curves crossing at $P$ are orthogonal when $m_1 m_2 = -1$, and the angle between them satisfies $\tan\phi = \left|\frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2}\right|$. Micro-check: for $y = x^2$ at $x = 2$ the point is $(2, 4)$, $m_T = 4$, $m_N = -1/4$, and the normal is $y - 4 = -\tfrac{1}{4}(x - 2)$, i.e. $y = -\tfrac{x}{4} + \tfrac{9}{2}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Monotonicity: Read the Sign of $f'$
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $f'(x) > 0$ on an interval means strictly increasing, $f'(x) < 0$ strictly decreasing; an ISOLATED zero of $f'$ where the sign does not change (like $x^3$ at $0$) does not break strict monotonicity. The working method is the sign table: find where $f' = 0$ or $f'$ fails, split the real line at those points, test one point per region, then read increasing/decreasing intervals straight off the table. Micro-check: $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$ has $f' = 3(x^2-1)$, negative on $(-1, 1)$ and positive outside, so $f$ increases on $(-\infty,-1) \cup (1,\infty)$ and decreases on $(-1,1)$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Critical Points and the Two Extrema Tests
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Critical points are interior $c$ with $f'(c) = 0$ or $f'(c)$ undefined — candidates, never verdicts. First-derivative test: the sign of $f'$ flipping $+ \to -$ at $c$ gives a local maximum, $- \to +$ a local minimum, no flip neither. Second-derivative test: at a stationary point $f''(c) < 0$ hilltop, $f''(c) > 0$ valley; if $f''(c) = 0$ fall back to the first-derivative test. Always convert the critical $x$ into the extremum VALUE $f(c)$ — JELET asks for values. Micro-check: $x^3 - 3x$ has critical points $\pm 1$; $f'' = 6x < 0$ at $x = -1$ gives local maximum value $f(-1) = 2$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Concavity and Points of Inflection
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $f''(x) > 0$ makes the graph concave up (holds water), $f''(x) < 0$ concave down. A point of inflection needs BOTH $f''(c) = 0$ (or undefined) AND a genuine sign change of $f''$ across $c$ — $f(x) = x^4$ has $f''(0) = 0$ yet $x = 0$ is a strict minimum, not an inflection. Micro-check: for $y = x^4 - 6x^2$, $y'' = 12x^2 - 12 = 0$ at $x = \pm 1$, and $y''$ changes sign at both — two inflection points, $(1, -5)$ and $(-1, -5)$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Global Extrema and the Word-Problem Recipe
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: On a closed interval $[a, b]$ the absolute maximum/minimum is found by evaluating $f$ at every critical point AND both endpoints, then comparing — endpoints win whenever $f$ is monotone across the interval. On open or split domains (like $x + \tfrac{1}{x}$ with $x \neq 0$), compare each branch separately: its local maximum $-2$ at $x = -1$ sits BELOW its local minimum $+2$ at $x = 1$. Word problems follow one recipe: model the quantity, differentiate, solve $f' = 0$, classify with $f''$, then answer the ASKED quantity (area, cost, volume — not the variable $x$). Micro-check: on $[0, \tfrac{\pi}{2}]$, $\sin x + \cos x$ peaks at $x = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$ with value $\sqrt{2}$.

keyDefinitions.definition: The tangent touches $y = f(x)$ at $P$ with slope $f'$; the normal is the perpendicular line through $P$ with slope $-1/f'$.
A function rising or falling across an interval as certified by the sign of $f'$.
Interior $c$ where $f'(c) = 0$ or $f'$ does not exist; the candidate list for extrema.
A value $f(c)$ greater (maximum) or smaller (minimum) than all nearby values of $f$.
The largest/smallest value over the WHOLE domain or interval — decided only after comparing candidates and endpoints.
A point where the curve changes concavity: $f''$ vanishes (or fails) AND changes sign there.
Concave up when $f'' > 0$ (valley shape), concave down when $f'' < 0$ (dome shape).
Curves whose tangents at an intersection are perpendicular: $m_1 m_2 = -1$.
Problems linking two time-varying quantities through the chain rule, $\frac{dY}{dt} = f'(x)\frac{dx}{dt}$.
The linear estimate $dy = f'(x)\,dx$ of the true change $\Delta y$ for small $\Delta x$.

mcqSelfTest.explanation: Critical points $\pm 1$; $f''(x) = 6x < 0$ at $x = -1$ gives a maximum with value $f(-1) = -1 + 3 = 2$.

mcqSelfTest.explanation: $f'(x) = 2x - 4 = 0$ at $x = 2$ inside $[0,3]$, and $f(2) = 1$ beats the endpoint values $f(0) = 5$, $f(3) = 2$.

mcqSelfTest.explanation: $y'' = 12x^2 - 12$ vanishes at $x = \pm 1$ and changes sign at both — two inflection points.

The curves $y = e^x$ and $y = e^{-x}$ intersect at $(0, 1)$. The product of their slopes there is:

memoryHooks: Tangent borrows $f'$, normal borrows $-1/f'$ — perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$.
Sign of $f'$ paints the graph: $+$ climbs, $-$ slides.
Critical points are candidates, not verdicts — always run a test.
$f'' = 0$ alone proves nothing — $x^4$ is flat at $0$ and still a minimum.
On a closed interval, endpoints always enter the max-min race.
Chain rule turns how-fast questions into $f'(x)\,dx/dt$.
Word problems end at the ASKED quantity — area or cost, not $x$.
An isolated zero of $f'$ ($x^3$ at $0$) does not break strict monotonicity.
$\Delta y \approx f'(x)\Delta x$ — small-change estimates in one line.
commonMistakes: Treating $f''(c) = 0$ as automatic inflection — $f(x) = x^4$ at $0$ is a strict minimum.
Forgetting endpoints on closed-interval absolute extrema; monotone functions peak at an end.
Reporting the critical $x$ instead of the extremum value $f(c)$ when the question asks for a value.
Flipping the normal slope without negating: $m_N = -1/m_T$, not $1/m_T$.
Classifying critical points without any test — $f'(c) = 0$ alone says nothing.
Declaring decrease from an isolated zero of $f'$ (like $x^3$ at $0$).
Using $\tan\phi = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2}$ without the modulus or missing the $1 + m_1m_2$ denominator.
In related rates, substituting the instantaneous value of the variable BEFORE differentiating.
On split domains ($x + 1/x$), comparing a local max with a local min across the domain hole.
examChecklist: Compute $f'(x_0)$ first; write the tangent equation with the actual point $(x_0, y_0)$ substituted.
Normals: negate the reciprocal; handle horizontal/vertical tangents separately.
Build the monotonicity sign table with one test point per region.
List ALL critical points ($f' = 0$ or undefined) before classifying.
Prefer the second-derivative test at stationary points; fall back to the first-derivative test when $f'' = 0$.
Absolute extrema on $[a, b]$: evaluate critical values AND $f(a)$, $f(b)$.
Inflection: demand BOTH $f'' = 0$ (or undefined) and a genuine sign change.
Related rates: differentiate first, substitute the instantaneous values last.
Orthogonality checks: verify $m_1 m_2 = -1$ at the actual intersection point.
Word problems: model, differentiate, classify, then restate the asked quantity with units.
Sanity-check one derivative computation before using it downstream.
